title: Penalty-Based First-Order Methods for Bilevel Optimization with Minimax and Constrained Lower-Level Problems
claim: Our method converges to far lower objective and constraint-violation error than baseline methods, which plateau or converge slowly.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row, shared x-axis, metrics in subcaptions
description: Three side-by-side line plots compare convergence of three methods over training iterations, measured in millions on the shared x-axis. A legend in panel (a) names FOP in blue, SMO in orange and Ours in green. Panel (a) plots the objective f(x1,y1). All methods reach about -450, but Ours drops fastest. Panel (b) plots the log10 duality gap p(x1,y1) - d(x1,y2). Ours falls to about -6 almost immediately and stays flat. FOP plateaus near -3.5 after step-like drops. SMO decreases slowly with spikes to about -3. Panel (c) plots the log10 norm of the positive part of the constraint violation. Ours sits near -6.5, FOP near -4 and SMO near -3.5. The green curve far below the others draws the eye first. Subcaptions use math notation.
caption: Performance for an instance with $(n,m,l)=(300,300,15)$ and tuned Lipschitz constants.
abstract: We study a class of bilevel optimization problems in which both the upper- and lower-level problems have minimax structures. This setting captures a broad range of emerging applications. Despite the extensive literature on bilevel optimization and minimax optimization separately, existing methods mainly focus on bilevel optimization with lower-level minimization problems, often under strong convexity assumptions, and are not directly applicable to the minimax lower-level setting considered here. To address this gap, we develop penalty-based first-order methods for bilevel minimax optimization without requiring strong convexity of the lower-level problem. In the deterministic setting, we establish that the proposed method finds a lifted $Îµ$-KKT point with $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-4})$ oracle complexity. We further show that bilevel problems with convex constrained lower-level minimization can be reformulated as special cases of our framework via Lagrangian duality, leading to an $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-4})$ complexity bound that improves upon the existing $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-7})$ result when the lower-level Slater's condition holds. Finally, we extend our approach to the stochastic setting, where only stochastic gradient oracles are available, and prove that the proposed stochastic method finds a nearly lifted $Îµ$-KKT point with $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-9})$ oracle complexity.
